ada: Quick sync: how should we handle lease TTL vs immediate revokes for abuse cases?
matt: Short TTLs + revocation pubsub. TTL gives natural expiry; pubsub gives kill switch.
zara: TTL-only is risky for active abuse. Add a nonce to leases so runtime can validate revocations.
jj: Agreed. Pubsub -> control-plane fanout to runtimes. Need auth + ordering guarantees. I'll bench.
olga: Also record revocation events in the ledger for audits and billing adjustments.
ada: Example admit_response sketch: {decision: "allow", lease_id: "L-123", nonce: "n-9", ttl_s: 30} 
matt: Revocation proto sketch: {lease_id: "L-123", nonce: "n-9", reason: "abuse", ts: 1710000000} 
jj: Implementation plan: prototype pubsub topic + lightweight runtime consumer; measure revoke->drop latencies end-to-end (<200ms target).
zara: Telemetry needs: revocation count, revoke->drop p50/95/99, expired-lease vs revoked-lease ratio.
ad a: Action: jj -> pubsub POC, matt -> admit_response proto, olga -> ledger revocation audit note, zara -> telemetry dashboard.
matt: +1
sre-bot: deploy-note: revocation-proto POC enabled on canary cluster 2026-04-10T12:00Z
